Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA Appoints New Senior Executive Amid Steady Growth in Spanish Automotive Sector

Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA, a major player in Spain's automotive components industry, announced the appointment of José María Ríos as its new Chief Operating Officer (COO) on Tuesday. The move comes as the company continues to strengthen its leadership team, aiming to reinforce its position in both domestic and international markets.

Ríos, who previously held senior operational roles at other automotive suppliers, brings more than 20 years of experience in manufacturing and supply chain management. His appointment is effective immediately. Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA, headquartered in Burgos, is known for its interior systems and has been expanding its footprint in new mobility solutions and smart technology integration.

In a statement, María Helena Antolín, Vice Chairwoman of Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA, expressed confidence in the new appointment. “José María’s extensive expertise in operational excellence and innovation aligns perfectly with our strategic vision. We are confident he will play a pivotal role in driving our ongoing transformation and delivering value to our customers worldwide,” she said.

Ríos will be responsible for overseeing all operational functions, including production, logistics, and quality assurance across the company’s facilities in Spain and abroad. Industry observers note that the appointment signals Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA’s commitment to furthering its competitiveness as the automotive sector undergoes significant technological changes.

“Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA has shown remarkable adaptability in recent years, especially in integrating advanced materials and digital solutions into their products,” commented Javier Gómez, an analyst with the Castile and León Industrial Forum. “Bringing on a COO with a strong background in operational efficiency suggests the company is gearing up for the next phase of growth.”

The company’s Burgos plant, one of the largest automotive component manufacturing sites in the region, employs more than 1,500 people and is viewed as a cornerstone of local industry. The regional trade union, Unión de Trabajadores de Castilla, welcomed the appointment. “We look forward to working closely with Mr. Ríos to ensure continued stability and opportunities for our workforce,” said union spokesperson Lucía Herrera.

Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA reported steady revenues in 2023, with a modest increase attributed to growing demand for custom interior solutions among European automakers. The company has also invested in sustainability initiatives, including energy efficiency upgrades at its main facilities.

As the Spanish automotive sector continues to recover from pandemic-era challenges, industry leaders like Grupo Antolin-Irausa SA are expected to play a crucial role in anchoring local economies and advancing innovation.
